45	## Plan-wide conventions (adopted from Sol round 3)
46	
47	1. **Five-column definition of done** for every capability: producer implemented → consumer wired → runtime activated → end-to-end tested → measured. "Implemented" alone means nothing; the historical failure mode was green at column 1 while column 3–4 were red.
48	2. **Green ladder:** unit → contract → cross-repo → installed-runtime → canary. No phase closes below cross-repo green; anything touching hooks/installs needs installed-runtime green.
49	3. **One typed client identity everywhere:** `claude_code | codex | mcp | api_worker | other`. Retires `host-adapter`/`ccx`/`claude` ad-hoc strings across Membrane providers, Forge adapters, and telemetry. Preferred mechanism: set `MEMBRANE_CLIENT` in each host's config (the adapter reads it first); the capability-set edit is fallback. Test pins the literal strings both adapters emit.
50	4. **Vocabulary rule:** agent-visible surfaces (headers, reasons, tool names, errors) say only Membrane/Cortex; compat aliases live behind adapters and in frozen telemetry keys. Governed by a **retired-vocabulary manifest** (YAML: term → replacement → explicit allowlist) whose gate scans all four repos + generated instructions + installed hook templates + the runtime skill-catalog export.
51	5. **Notifications are cache invalidation, never authority.** Freshness authority is always a read-through proof of the Cortex generation envelope + watcher/barrier state.
52	6. **Runtime stores reconcile with tombstones.** Any repo→store sync (skills, rules, catalogs) carries `catalogGeneration`, `sourceTreeDigest`, entries, and tombstones; sync deletes retired entries; doctor/CI diffs source vs runtime export. This is the structural fix for `glass`/`blueprint` ghosts — grep of Git can never prove runtime state.

61	- **E2E-4 headless rules:** non-self-loading client → full static policy once at session start; unchanged turns deliver zero static bytes; changed policy invalidates.

Native-loading hosts get rules marked delivered-by-host, never serialized.
79	- **2.4 Delivery model.** Session start: membrane-first routing line + catalog digest + memory/Taste index availability + health (+ full rules only for headless). Task start/shift: automatic `membrane_context` pull (Taste rules, memories, doc spine, Cortex slices). Continuation: nothing unchanged. External change: invalidation/changed-slice line only ("Cortex generation changed for HR — re-pull"). Explicit request: `membrane_context` always available. The 1,500-byte truncation question dissolves — nothing bulk rides the prompt.
80	- **2.5 Resident service (M5).** Per-prompt cold `node client.mjs` spawn → calls into the resident gateway. Removes the load-induced `packet: null` failures (observed again this session, defect 28).
81	- **2.6 Decision-point affordance (M6).** PreToolUse route: exact-file reads/greps pass; broad discovery greps get a `membrane_context` suggestion; cross-repo discovery routes through Membrane; Membrane miss → fallback allowed, omission recorded. The passive instruction alone demonstrably fails.
82	- **2.7 One workspace watcher, Membrane-resident (Adrian's decision 2026-08-04).** The resident Membrane service hosts the single watcher process; Cortex's `WatchSupervisor` already multiplexes every repo actor in one process (supervisor.mjs:50 — one FSEvents subscription per root, no per-repo processes), so residency is supervision of that one process plus a workspace-root actor (ignore-globbed for caches), not a rewrite. Routing by path: repo code/doc events → Cortex's existing delta pipeline (Cortex library code remains the only writer/interpreter of graph.db — Membrane routes, never reimplements, or defect 27 recurs mirrored); `tools/skills/**/SKILL.md` → the reconciling `ingest_skills` (prune included); rules/docs sources → `docs-sync` + an agent-rules `check` drift warning. Freshness authority stays read-through per convention 5 — the watcher is delivery speed, never truth; a dead watcher is 1.2's honest `stale` verdict, which is a different failure class from the silent adapt/glass ghosts (no staleness signal at all) and is precisely why watcher-fed catalogs remain safe. Hash-on-read survives as the read-through proof and the post-downtime reconcile (reconcile.mjs), not as a competing mechanism. This subsumes the "who runs ingest-skills/docs-sync" gap: the watcher runs them.

99	- **5.1 `TranscriptEventV1` layer** (`tools/lib/orthic_transcripts/`): all seven host adapters (Claude + Codex), byte spans (rowIndex, byteStart/End, blockIndex, sequence), event identity = prefix-digest+span+kind+payload, frozen prefix receipts binding host+sessionId+transcriptId+prefixLength+prefixDigest+parser implementation digest, flags (synthetic/meta/privateReasoningOmitted/redacted).

101	- **5.3 Taste** (mission unchanged): corrections + locked decisions → durable scoped rules with exact-span provenance → Crypt → `membrane_context`. Keep authority/privacy strengths (user-origin isolation, synthetic/meta filters, health-domain exclusion, lifecycle states). Fix: keep surrounding context of corrections. Never authoritative: assistant narration, tool output, repo prose, Insights findings.
102	- **5.4 Membrane→Morph transport (MH6).** Build the HTTP route over `EventTransport` (`event_ingestion.py:9`) + `query_by_id(event_id)` so taste candidates can fetch content. This is where 5.3's context fix physically lands.

Detectors: claimed-verified-then-corrected, repeated ask, visible frustration, verification claim without tool evidence, ignored tool failure, degraded-provider-treated-as-success, false not-found, unproductive broad searching, wrong repo/subsystem, stale terminology surfacing, silent scope narrowing, omitted requirement, unaccepted plan change, tests-that-cannot-fail, cross-agent repeats, forge-opened-never-closed, guard firings, user-asks-why-missed / postmortem-requested. 104	- **5.6 Contract tests.** Real transcripts from both hosts round-trip through all three projections with identical event IDs/spans (E2E-7). No phrase-greps. Naming hygiene: settle `morph` vs `adapt`.

106	## Phase 6 — Forge hardening
107	
108	- **6.1 Rubric contract (S1, rescoped).** `close()` never reads a rubric (`core.js:127`) — codify: verify evaluates and persists the rubric; close closes only that verified rubric/version; a rubric supplied to close is explicitly rejected ("rubric belongs to verify"), never silently ignored; unverified cannot close. Contract test, not grep.
109	- **6.2 Locked-domain wiring (S2, rescoped).** Mechanism exists (`lib/locked-domain.js`); work = wire into each host's Stop hook, declare this workspace's domains, add the claims-verified-without-closed-run_id trigger plus claim-phrase triggers ("verified"/"validated"/"fully fixed" in an agent completion claim require a verification receipt), delete the "over two changed files" prose.
110	- **6.3 Installation qualification matrix (S3+).** Per host: discoverable, tools listed, assess→verify→close, Stop hook result, correct identity, no duplicated Membrane block (E2E-8). Source can't prove installs; the harness does.
111	- **6.4 Test hygiene (S4).** `git rm forge/test/codex-profile.test.mjs` (classifier-blocked for agents — Adrian's one-liner) + guard: Forge tests read only their own repo; external prose becomes frozen local fixtures.
112	- **6.5 Dispatcher consolidation (S5, after health).** One dispatcher per host event (SessionStart/UserPrompt/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop) with per-handler latency records and a total budget. A verifier that delays prompts gets bypassed.
113	- **6.6 Time-accounting loop (tasklist → rhook → Forge).** Plans carry one realistic total-minutes number plus per-task minute spans accounting for the whole total, derived from scope (lines × rate + overhead), no low/high ranges; parallelize independent tasks by default (serial steps must justify blocking). tasklist declares the budget; rhook computes actual active minutes from its existing tool-call timestamps (the model never self-reports actuals — the hook clock is the receipt); Forge close requires the plan-vs-actual receipt and scores variance symmetrically — beyond ±10% in either direction (overquote or overrun) is a recorded miss. Breach = stop & report, never silent revision; external wait excluded from active minutes. Subagents are never force-closed unless running unbounded — report estimated remaining time instead. Estimate derivations must be producible on demand; unjustifiable numbers are fudged and rejected. Rates come from measured session history once receipts accumulate. **Status 2026-08-04: producer implemented + consumer wired + unit/contract green** (tasklist budget fields + validator; Membrane `ForgeToolOnly` scope, `duration_ms` wire field, `:query-forge-time` route; Forge `time-accounting.js` + async `close()` recording non-blocking `time_variance`; cargo + npm suites green). **Not yet runtime-activated/e2e-tested**: live tasklist→close round-trip against the resident service — per convention 1, this is columns 1–2 done, 3–5 open. **Correction 2026-08-04 (found by Adrian, not by any test):** the rule edit landed in `docs/agent-rules/workspace.md` but `tools/agent-rules/manage.py sync` was never run, so all 19 generated overlays — including the root `AGENTS.md` that Codex actually reads — still served the retired "low/likely/high ETA" text; a Codex agent kept emitting ranges because it was obeying the rule it was given. Separately the wording "per-task minute spans" was itself ambiguous and read as durations (`15–25 min`) rather than elapsed-clock offsets (`minute 3–20`). Both fixed; validator now rejects duration/range formats and derives the total as the last minute any step runs. **Second correction (Adrian, same day):** the rewrite silently dropped the file/line ceilings the retired rule had, and `lines × rate + overhead` was itself a bad model — measured against a real lane (477 added lines), code generation ran ~30–95 lines/min while wall clock was dominated by inspect/compile/test/smoke, so a single "overhead" term absorbed the actual work and made the total unfalsifiable. 116	  - **Mutation testing on changed lines.** Inject faults into the diff's own lines; a surviving mutant means the test cannot fail. This is the *preventive* twin of Insights' `tests-that-cannot-fail` detector (5.5), which only reports the failure after it has already shipped.
117	  - **Changed-lines-only coverage.** Coverage measured on the diff, never repo-wide — a whole-repo percentage moves too slowly to gate anything and punishes untouched legacy code.
118	  - **Test-order independence.** See 7.5; the same runner flag serves both.

Requirement: one query spec, one result schema, one golden-test set — not RPC for its own sake.
- **3.3 Abstention.** Delete cohort (`blueprint.py:307-333`) and `_pin_fresh_candidate` (`:553-564`). - **3.4 Contract drift fixes.** Self-describing hash prefixes; publish the resolver actually executed (executable test per emitted command); adopt name-equality exactness.

## Phase 4 — Cross-repository retrieval

- **4.1 `RepositoryCatalogEntryV1`.** Extend the existing catalog: repoId, aliases (HR/HeardRight, CR/CodeRight, MR…), origin, rootBinding, graphPath, cortexGenerationId, manifestDigest, sourceCommit, watcherState (`current|degraded|stale|unwatched`), capabilities, grantPolicy. Cortex publishes the descriptor (C3); Membrane populates.
- **4.2 Scoped federation.** `membrane_context(query, scope="workspace"|repo)`: resolve likely repos via aliases/dependencies → request one bounded slice per target graph → fuse with Taste/memory/rules/git → return references + receipts → resolve source only for admitted references. ## Phase 5 — Shared transcript substrate (Morph + Handoff + Insights)

- **5.1 `TranscriptEventV1` layer** (`tools/lib/orthic_transcripts/`): all seven host adapters (Claude + Codex), byte spans (rowIndex, byteStart/End, blockIndex, sequence), event identity = prefix-digest+span+kind+payload, frozen prefix receipts binding host+sessionId+transcriptId+prefixLength+prefixDigest+parser implementation digest, flags (synthetic/meta/privateReasoningOmitted/redacted).
- **5.2 Handoff on the layer**, fixing in one pass (defect 21 + review set): session ID bound into receipt; exact-match resolution (no `requested_id not in path.name`); (call_id, occurrence) pairing; class-priority admission replacing the six-pair reducer — order: unresolved failures > mutations > failed verification > open user requests > decisions/constraints > successful read-only (cap squeezes only the last class); structured failure detection with regex fallback; planning ops not classified as mutations; fingerprint-set dedup; multi-block-intact segmentation; tail-preserving truncation.
- **5.3 Taste** (mission unchanged): corrections + locked decisions → durable scoped rules with exact-span provenance → Crypt → `membrane_context`. Keep authority/privacy strengths (user-origin isolation, synthetic/meta filters, health-domain exclusion, lifecycle states). Fix: keep surrounding context of corrections. Never authoritative: assistant narration, tool output, repo prose, Insights findings.
- **5.4 Membrane→Morph transport (MH6).** Build the HTTP route over `EventTransport` (`event_ingestion.py:9`) + `query_by_id(event_id)` so taste candidates can fetch content. This is where 5.3's context fix physically lands.
- **5.5 Insights (greenfield, 1–2 weeks).** Customer: Adrian. Writes nothing to Membrane/Taste; automates nothing. Detectors: claimed-verified-then-corrected, repeated ask, visible frustration, verification claim without tool evidence, ignored tool failure, degraded-provider-treated-as-success, false not-found, unproductive broad searching, wrong repo/subsystem, stale terminology surfacing, silent scope narrowing, omitted requirement, unaccepted plan change, tests-that-cannot-fail, cross-agent repeats, forge-opened-never-closed, guard firings, user-asks-why-missed / postmortem-requested. Output: `morph insights` report of `FailureCardV1` (severity, confidence, first/lastSeen, recurrenceCount, agents/hosts/sessions/repos, taskSummary, userExpectation, observedFailure, byte-span evidence excerpts, clearly-labelled likelyMechanism + suggestedRemediations, userDisposition). Honest limit stated in-product: only observable failure signals are detectable.
- **5.6 Contract tests.** Real transcripts from both hosts round-trip through all three projections with identical event IDs/spans (E2E-7). No phrase-greps. Naming hygiene: settle `morph` vs `adapt`.

## Phase 6 — Forge hardening

- **6.1 Rubric contract (S1, rescoped).** `close()` never reads a rubric (`core.js:127`) — codify: verify evaluates and persists the rubric; close closes only that verified rubric/version; a rubric supplied to close is explicitly rejected ("rubric belongs to verify"), never silently ignored; unverified cannot close. Contract test, not grep.
- **6.2 Locked-domain wiring (S2, rescoped).** Mechanism exists (`lib/locked-domain.js`); work = wire into each host's Stop hook, declare this workspace's domains, add the claims-verified-without-closed-run_id trigger plus claim-phrase triggers ("verified"/"validated"/"fully fixed" in an agent completion claim require a verification receipt), delete the "over two changed files" prose.
- **6.3 Installation qualification matrix (S3+).** Per host: discoverable, tools listed, assess→verify→close, Stop hook result, correct identity, no duplicated Membrane block (E2E-8). Source can't prove installs; the harness does.
- **6.4 Test hygiene (S4).** `git rm forge/test/codex-profile.test.mjs` (classifier-blocked for agents — Adrian's one-liner) + guard: Forge tests read only their own repo; external prose becomes frozen local fixtures.
- **6.5 Dispatcher consolidation (S5, after health).** One dispatcher per host event (SessionStart/UserPrompt/PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop) with per-handler latency records and a total budget. A verifier that delays prompts gets bypassed.
- **6.6 Time-accounting loop (tasklist → rhook → Forge).** Plans carry one realistic total-minutes number plus per-task minute spans accounting for the whole total, derived from scope (lines × rate + overhead), no low/high ranges; parallelize independent tasks by default (serial steps must justify blocking). tasklist declares the budget; rhook computes actual active minutes from its existing tool-call timestamps (the model never self-reports actuals — the hook clock is the receipt); Forge close requires the plan-vs-actual receipt and scores variance symmetrically — beyond ±10% in either direction (overquote or overrun) is a recorded miss. Breach = stop & report, never silent revision; external wait excluded from active minutes. Subagents are never force-closed unless running unbounded — report estimated remaining time instead. Estimate derivations must be producible on demand; unjustifiable numbers are fudged and rejected. Rates come from measured session history once receipts accumulate. **Status 2026-08-04: producer implemented + consumer wired + unit/contract green** (tasklist budget fields + validator; Membrane `ForgeToolOnly` scope, `duration_ms` wire field, `:query-forge-time` route; Forge `time-accounting.js` + async `close()` recording non-blocking `time_variance`; cargo + npm suites green). **Not yet runtime-activated/e2e-tested**: live tasklist→close round-trip against the resident service — per convention 1, this is columns 1–2 done, 3–5 open. **Correction 2026-08-04 (found by Adrian, not by any test):** the rule edit landed in `docs/agent-rules/workspace.md` but `tools/agent-rules/manage.py sync` was never run, so all 19 generated overlays — including the root `AGENTS.md` that Codex actually reads — still served the retired "low/likely/high ETA" text; a Codex agent kept emitting ranges because it was obeying the rule it was given. Separately the wording "per-task minute spans" was itself ambiguous and read as durations (`15–25 min`) rather than elapsed-clock offsets (`minute 3–20`). Both fixed; validator now rejects duration/range formats and derives the total as the last minute any step runs. **Second correction (Adrian, same day):** the rewrite silently dropped the file/line ceilings the retired rule had, and `lines × rate + overhead` was itself a bad model — measured against a real lane (477 added lines), code generation ran ~30–95 lines/min while wall clock was dominated by inspect/compile/test/smoke, so a single "overhead" term absorbed the actual work and made the total unfalsifiable. Replaced with named activity components per step (`code=11, compile=8, test=12, inspect=12`) that must sum to the step's span, a banned-label list (overhead/buffer/contingency/misc/slack/other), a rejected sub-10 lines-per-minute rate, and a check that declared code minutes follow from lines ÷ rate. **Standing lesson: editing a rule source is not shipping a rule — the generator run is the delivery step, and nothing currently forces it.** Candidate guard: fail `agent-rules check` from a pre-commit/CI path (`generated-lock.json` drift already detects it), same shape as convention 6.

- **6.7 Evidence gauntlet (borrowed from [old-coder](https://github.com/AmazingAng/old-coder); diff-scoped).** Three mechanical check kinds the stack currently lacks, all bounded to the frozen diff so cost stays proportional:
  - **Mutation testing on changed lines.** Inject faults into the diff's own lines; a surviving mutant means the test cannot fail. This is the *preventive* twin of Insights' `tests-that-cannot-fail` detector (5.5), which only reports the failure after it has already shipped.
  - **Changed-lines-only coverage.** Coverage measured on the diff, never repo-wide — a whole-repo percentage moves too slowly to gate anything and punishes untouched legacy code.
  - **Test-order independence.** See 7.5; the same runner flag serves both.
  Integration rule: gauntlet output enters Forge as `checks` with `executor: host` plus a receipt — never as model-authored claims — so existing trust-class and issuer-derived-field enforcement applies unchanged. Standing anti-gaming constraint, stated in the check spec: never weaken a test to make the gauntlet pass, never report an unrun check as passed, label unverified findings as unverified. Reports take old-coder's EVIDENCE shape: one rerunnable command, real metrics, pass/fail per layer — which also satisfies the workspace "one small runnable check" rule with a standard format instead of an ad-hoc one. Home: `/commit`'s diff-frozen gate, surfaced through Forge check specs.

## Phase 7 — Cortex internals (interleavable; must not delay Phases 1–3)
